rubrics.criterion: After the patch, no interface declaration in the package forces a pipeline participant to provide text capabilities that the participant does not perform: the uniform contract that coupled the whole phase catalogue (substitutions, ASCII normalization, casing, both truncations, separator cleanup, timestamp suffix, plus the diagnostics and validation capabilities) onto every registered stage is gone, or is decomposed so that no participant satisfies capabilities it does not own through own or inherited pass-through method bodies.
rubrics.rationale: This is the core obligation of the case: the injection made each of the seven stage types (and the shared default carrier) satisfy one twelve-capability interface, most of them via `return s` stubs. A solver patch resolves the case only when that forced coupling no longer exists in any shape, whether the contract was split into focused groupings or removed entirely.

rubrics.criterion: After the patch, no consumer that advances slug generation phases accepts a value typed by a capability contract that is broader than the capability set that consumer actually invokes through it; the phase-advancing code either calls the phase-owning participant directly or through a contract containing only capabilities it uses.
rubrics.rationale: The injected applyStages walks full-contract values in ten separate phase loops, each invoking exactly one capability. Fixing only the stage side while leaving consumers processing full-capability values would preserve the client half of the segregation problem, so the consumer side must be judged independently.

rubrics.criterion: After the patch, no participant of the package is required to provide a capability that no consumer of that capability's contract ever invokes, and the slug shape validation used by the exported validation function is reached directly (as a function or on a concrete implementor) instead of being imposed as a required capability on a set of unrelated participants.
rubrics.rationale: Two capabilities of the injected contract were never dispatched through it: the diagnostics stage-name provider (its consumer surface was never built) and shape validation (executed only through the concrete shared carrier from the exported IsSlug). A repair that re-imposes either obligation on future participants, for instance by making it a required method of a new common grouping, has not resolved this part of the case.

rubrics.criterion: The slug generation entry point (the MakeLang path) is rewired to whatever structure replaces the pipeline participants, and it still performs the complete ordered phase sequence with the trim of the input, producing the pipeline phases in the same order as before the patch.
rubrics.rationale: MakeLang was turned into a thin wrapper over the injected pipeline; any sound repair must reconnect it to the replacement structure. A solver that leaves the generation function calling removed machinery, or drops the trim/phase chaining, fails this outcome regardless of how well the contract itself was treated.

rubrics.criterion: The language substitution logic that the pipeline's language participant owned remains reachable from the generation path and complete: every language code family previously accepted (including the multi-alias and country-code cases such as the Greek, Kazakh and Brazilian Portuguese aliases) still selects its own substitution table, and unknown languages still fall back to the English table.
rubrics.rationale: The language dispatch was relocated into a contract participant in the languages file; it is the largest independent responsibility in the diff and the easiest to lose track of while dissolving the contract. This outcome is about preservation of the dispatch itself, not about where it lives.

rubrics.criterion: Every option-conditioned phase still consults its package option variable with the same effect as before the patch: casing follows Lowercase, the two truncation modes follow EnableSmartTruncate and MaxLength (both the word-boundary cut and the unconditional cut), dash collapsing follows DisableMultipleDashTrim, edge trimming follows DisableEndsTrim, and the suffix phase follows AppendTimestamp.
rubrics.rationale: The injected participants internalized the package option conditionals that previously lived in the generation function. A repair that rebuilds truncation, cleanup or suffixing without preserving each option's trigger conditions changes behavior even when the phases themselves stay present.

rubrics.criterion: Obsolete machinery of the dissolved design is removed rather than left behind: no unreferenced stage registry, shared default carrier with pass-through method bodies, or hand-written pass-through participant remains in the package after the repair.
rubrics.rationale: The injection introduced a registry of stage values, a shared default type whose only job was propping up the fat contract, and one participant spelling out every pass-through by hand. Keeping any of these as dead scaffolding after the contract is gone is an incomplete cleanup specific to this instance.

rubrics.criterion: Capability implementations whose only purpose was satisfying the uniform contract, in particular the per-participant diagnostics name providers and participant-level validation members that no longer have any caller, are deleted together with the contract instead of surviving as unused methods.
rubrics.rationale: These members existed only because the interface required them of every participant. They produce no externally observable behavior, so they are exactly the kind of ceremonial residue this case wants gone, while a patch that leaves one or two behind is only partially unclean.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not alter the ordering or content of the generation phases in a way that changes output, for example applying the string substitution map before the rune substitution map, running ASCII normalization after unauthorized-symbol replacement, truncating before all other phases run, applying the timestamp suffix before trimming and truncation, or swapping the two truncation modes.
rubrics.rationale: These are the concrete silent-corruption paths for this package: the phase order and the runes-before-strings rule are pinned by existing tests, but a patch that reorders phases inside a rewritten structure may still compile and partially pass while producing different slugs for inputs the suite exercises lightly.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not eliminate phase behavior in order to eliminate obligations, for example dropping the hard truncation performed when smart truncation is disabled, the dash collapsing, the edge trimming, the timestamp suffix, or the custom substitution pass, under the justification that the participant carrying it was part of the contract machinery.
rubrics.rationale: All phase logic was placed inside contract participants by the injection, so a lazy repair can delete participants wholesale and mistake removed capabilities for removed ceremony. Deleting required behavior is not a valid interface-segregation repair for this package.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not break the compilation contract around the package boundary: the exported functions keep their signatures, the option variables keep their names and types, and the internal helpers that the package's own benchmarks invoke directly (the word-boundary truncation helper in particular) remain callable as package-level functions with the same call shape.
rubrics.rationale: The package's own test suite lives in the same package and calls the unexported truncation helper by name, so restructuring it into a method or removing it breaks the suite build. A solver must keep the internal surface the tests bind to even while rewriting how the generation path is organized.
